1: Lo, the hope of him is found a liar, Also at his appearance is not one cast down?
2: None so fierce that he doth awake him, And who is he before Me stationeth himself?
3: Who hath brought before Me and I repay? Under the whole heavens it is mine.
4: I do not keep silent concerning his parts, And the matter of might, And the grace of his arrangement.
5: Who hath uncovered the face of his clothing? Within his double bridle who doth enter?
6: The doors of his face who hath opened? Round about his teeth are terrible.
7: A pride--strong ones of shields, Shut up--a close seal.
8: One unto another they draw nigh, And air doth not enter between them.
9: One unto another they adhere, They stick together and are not separated.
10: His sneezings cause light to shine, And his eyes are as the eyelids of the dawn.
11: Out of his mouth do flames go, sparks of fire escape.
12: Out of his nostrils goeth forth smoke, As a blown pot and reeds.
13: His breath setteth coals on fire, And a flame from his mouth goeth forth.
14: In his neck lodge doth strength, And before him doth grief exult.
15: The flakes of his flesh have adhered--Firm upon him--it is not moved.
16: His heart is firm as a stone, Yea, firm as the lower piece.
17: From his rising are the mighty afraid, From breakings they keep themselves free.
18: The sword of his overtaker standeth not, Spear--dart--and lance.
19: He reckoneth iron as straw, brass as rotten wood.
20: The son of the bow doth not cause him to flee, Turned by him into stubble are stones of the sling.
21: As stubble have darts been reckoned, And he laugheth at the shaking of a javelin.
22: Under him are sharp points of clay, He spreadeth gold on the mire.
23: He causeth to boil as a pot the deep, The sea he maketh as a pot of ointment.
24: After him he causeth a path to shine, One thinketh the deep to be hoary.
25: There is not on the earth his like, That is made without terror.
26: Every high thing he doth see, He is king over all sons of pride.
